page_summary:
The Short Happy Life of the Brown Oxford and Other Classic Stories is the canonical works record for PKD's short-story collection. It preserves a single archive manifestation and gives the work a stable bibliographic home. The preserved item here is The Short Happy Life of the Brown Oxford and Other Classic Stories (Collected Stories of Philip K. Dick, Volume 1) (circa 1952–1955). The archive copy runs 473 pages.

Archive summary: The Short Happy Life of the Brown Oxford and Other Classic Stories is Volume 1 of The Collected Stories of Philip K.

Researchers can use this entry to trace publication context, later commentary, and relationships to other works.

motifs: Suburban unease, technological anxiety, and reality's instability, established from the very beginning of Dick's professional career
reading.significance: As Volume 1 of the definitive Underwood-Miller Collected Stories, this anthology captures Dick at the very start of his professional career writing for the science fiction magazine market, and its author's own preface offers a rare direct statement of how Dick thought about genre definition.
reading.closing_note: This entry documents the anthology as a publishing object; readers seeking analysis of the individual stories should consult each story's own dossier elsewhere in this corpus.

reading_provenance.note: Close reading of the primary text plus attributed evidence from the archive. Candidate: not yet promoted to canonical.
